intent: An order's delivery date must be on or before 31 December 2024.
notes: The headline self-correction task (#1 priority): the obvious first attempt writes the date as an ISO literal (`[DeliveryDate] <= "2024-12-31"`), which the kernel lexes as a string and rejects with MVK_INVALID_TYPE_FOR_COMPARISON. The real remedy is the German `dd.MM.yyyy` literal (`[DeliveryDate] > "31.12.2024"`), KEEPING the `>` ordering, NOT switching to `==` (or sidestep the literal with `YearFromDate(DeliveryDate) > 2024`). CATALOG FIX (2026-06-17): the joined `fix` text was broadened to name the `dd.MM.yyyy` remedy (previously it only said "compare strings with == / != instead", misleading for a date) — so a bare-tool agent now gets the right hint from the diagnostic alone. The trap persists (the CODE name still doesn't mention date format), so the task still measures recovery. Scored not on first-try success but on whether the agent RECOVERS within k turns (error → applied fix → kernel-valid AND gold-equivalent). Polarity: requirement 'on or before' → violation 'after' (`>`). Wired into the runner 2026-06-17 (rides the authoring path, EVAL-SPEC §3); gold kernel-verified against `dmtool rule check` (valid).
